summary: Streets that climb hills: crossings that tilt, lots that level themselves with step walls, and map imports on real ground heights. Also lighter corners and floors, and levels that open without asking to be saved.
highlights: [Crossings on sloped streets](/core-actors/streets-network#crossings-on-slopes) tilt with the hill, and a climbing street runs through them in one smooth curve instead of a flat shelf at each crossing. Hilltops, valleys and flat networks stay level, and a side street never banks the main road.

Lot Elevation is now called [Lot Height](/core-actors/streets-network#lot-height-choices), with clearer choices (Follow Slope, Level at Low Side, Level at High Side) and two new ones: **Level at Main Street**, and **Auto**, which follows gentle slopes up to **Auto Slope Limit** (4 %) and uses **Steeper Than the Limit** above it. New networks start on Auto; saved networks keep Follow Slope. SA Subdivide Lots uses the same names.

[Step Walls](/core-actors/streets-network#step-walls) (under Sidewalks): wherever a lot stands above or below the street beside it, a wall now closes the gap, with its texture kept level along the lot edge. Pick **Step Wall Material** and **Step Wall Texture Height**, or switch it off when your own PCG graph builds those walls. On for new networks, off for saved ones.

[Import Map](/core-actors/import-map#ground-heights) has a **Ground heights** option (off by default): roads, map areas and buildings are set on real terrain heights, downloaded once per place. Bridges and tunnels span between their ends, and each building stands on the lowest ground under it.

[SA Get Lots](/pcg/node-reference#sa-get-lots) flags each lot edge that stands above its street (SA_EdgeRaised), and SA_LotElevation reports MainStreet for lots levelled at their main street. SA Filter Spline Edges on SA_EdgeRaised splits a lot outline into raised and sunken runs, for walls and railings.

**Corner Segment Length** on each Streets lot layer ([Corner Pads](/core-actors/streets-network#sidewalks-and-lot-ground)) sets how long each straight piece of a rounded street corner is. Raise it for lighter meshes on big map imports; 0 keeps today's automatic detail.

[Flat floors](/authoring/floors-roofs#floor-surface) and flat lot ground in one color are now just their outline, the same clean polygons roofs get. Extra points inside are added only where they change something: an outline that isn't flat, or an Edges Color that differs from the Fill Color. Facade Kit `_Fast` caps get lighter automatically; for other floors and lot layers whose material ignores vertex color, set Edges Color to the Fill Color.

Opening a level no longer asks you to save it just because its Runtime Spline Architect actors were rebuilt. The rebuild also no longer re-runs the level's PCG graphs, which keep the output saved with the level; press **Generate** on a PCG volume if its presets or meshes changed since the level was last saved. Anything you change while the rebuild runs still counts as unsaved. `sa.KeepLevelCleanAfterLoad 0` brings back the old behavior.
Opening the same level again in one editor session always rebuilds its Runtime actors; an unrelated update still in progress could skip it before.
A baked Building's preset source stays locked even when it was empty: assigning a preset table through Python or paste is now put back like every other edit to a baked actor.
notes: Saved Streets networks keep Follow Slope and have Step Walls off, so their lots look the same after the update. Only new networks start on Auto with Step Walls on. **Reset to Streets Defaults** switches a network to both.
Sloped streets change in saved networks too: their crossings tilt, and with Z Ramp on Auto a street climbs in one smooth curve instead of levelling out at every point. Flat streets are unchanged.

Existing imports keep their flat heights. Ground heights applies to imports made with it ticked. Its height data comes from Terrain Tiles, which needs a [credit line](/core-actors/import-map#credit-the-height-data) wherever you show or ship such an import.
Floors and lot ground rebuild with the lighter outline-only mesh the next time an actor generates; baked output keeps its old mesh until you rebake.
The 6.2.1 example project reads SA_EdgeRaised and the new Lot Height and Step Walls settings, so it needs this plugin version.

summary: Import real buildings from OpenStreetMap, make fast facade copies of your Building presets, build sloped roofs on irregular footprints, and choose whether baked meshes use Nanite.
highlights: [Import Map](/core-actors/import-map#buildings) brings in the buildings of a real place. Each one becomes a Building in a style from your Building preset tables, with its floors fitted to its map height. Touching buildings, such as row houses, share one wall. Keep one actor per building, one per lot, or one for all, or import footprints only for PCG. Underground buildings are skipped, and **Skip buildings outside lots** leaves out buildings that stand on no street lot. Replacing an import builds its buildings again from the map and does not keep edits.

The Import Map window is organised into **Roads**, **Areas** and **Buildings** tabs, each with its own limit. The search box suggests places as you type and reads pasted coordinates and plus codes. **Recent** returns to places you visited with their boundaries, and one **Map data** menu holds downloads, files and cleanup. Map data your project already holds is used for you, and downloads and the first reading of a file can be cancelled.
A mapped area the import cannot use is skipped and listed in Diagnostics, instead of stopping the import.
Areas and building outlines are read for the place you are looking at and cached in small tiles. There is no multi-gigabyte index to wait for and no Prepare outlines step.

New PCG node [SA Get Map Buildings](/pcg/node-reference#sa-get-map-buildings) reads imported buildings with their height, style and kind. SA Spawn Building can build each input in its own style and fit its height, and SA Get Lots reports how much of each lot real buildings already cover.

[Make Facade Kit](/authoring/facade-kit) turns a Building preset into a fast copy made of flat textured planes, for big map imports. Repeated floors share one photo, a Parallax switch makes windows look set into the wall, and a batch can be cancelled.
Sloped roofs on footprints with narrow wings, notches and nearly parallel walls now get proper hips and valleys instead of a flat roof.

The new project setting [Baked Mesh Nanite](/production/baking#nanite-on-baked-meshes) (Match Project, Always or Never) decides whether the shapes Spline Architect builds when you bake use Nanite. Lightmap UVs for those shapes follow the project's static lighting setting, copies of your own meshes follow the source mesh's Nanite setting, and Bake and Rebake are faster.
AI assistants can include buildings when they import a map area.
notes: Baked meshes now follow the project's Nanite setting on the next bake or rebake, and existing bakes stay as they are until then. Set **Baked Mesh Nanite** to **Never** to keep them as before.
Existing frozen bakes keep their old roofs until you rebake them.

Old map index files delete themselves. The large area index files that 6.1 kept under Saved/SplineArchitect/MapData are removed after the first successful read of a place, so that folder shrinks without any action from you.

summary: Work with AI assistants, import real streets from OpenStreetMap, keep baked output frozen until you unbake it, and set up Streets from a clearer Details panel.
highlights: Work with AI assistants through Unreal Engine's optional Model Context Protocol plugin. Assistants can place Spline Architect actors, apply presets, edit streets, import map sources, run SA PCG nodes, and convert results through the editor's own tools.
Import real streets and land areas from OpenStreetMap. Add a map file you already have, or download a regional extract after confirming its size.

Baked output stays frozen until you unbake it. Presets and spline shape are read-only while baked; moving or rotating the whole actor is still allowed. Editing a shared preset no longer discards other actors' bakes.
See which actors use a shared preset that changed since their last bake, and update them all with **Rebake out-of-date actors**.
SA PCG nodes can sample the floor and roof surfaces of baked Walls, Buildings, and Curves. Baked Streets networks restore their PCG data in a game world.

Streets ships with default appearance settings and portable sidewalk materials. Junctions, sidewalk corners, and sidewalk UVs are cleaner, and viewport editing works the same way across nodes, segments, and junctions.

A reorganized Streets Network Details panel: **Streets**, **Sidewalks & Lot Ground**, **Lots**, **Output & Baking** and a folded **Advanced** section, with settings named for what they build (Sidewalk Width, Curb Height, Corner Radius). **Reset to Streets Defaults** restores the look of a newly placed network in one undoable step.
New **Minimum Road Width** on the Streets Network widens every thinner road - including imported map roads - without re-importing. Roads you set by hand keep their width.
SA Edge Placer's new **Stay Upright** (on by default) keeps buildings and props level on sloped streets instead of tilting with the road.
SA Get Road Crossings reports **SA_NodeDegree**, so traffic lights and crossing signals go only where three or more roads meet.

The example project gains **PCG_SA_OSMCity**, a drop-in city graph: drag it onto any Streets network for buildings, parked cars, traffic lights, square-pot street trees, street lights, rooftop water towers, construction sites and alleys, all tuned from the Details panel. **L_SA_OSMCity** shows it on an imported Brooklyn map.
AI assistants can expose a PCG node's mesh list - or any number or on/off setting - as a graph parameter, so designers swap meshes and tune spacings from the Details panel without opening the graph.
Fixed: with sidewalks enabled, many lots of an imported map could come out empty; lots too narrow for their sidewalk are now built as plain ground.
Fixed: Import Map now offers the region download before any map source is set up.
Lot extrusions gain inset and upper bevel profiles.

Fixed: SA Edge Placer rows with a Lateral Offset, such as buildings or fences set back behind a sidewalk, ran past lot corners onto the neighbouring sidewalk; they now stop at the inner corner, and with Fit Inside Shape a deep building at a sharp corner no longer reaches into the other street's sidewalk.
Fixed: thin roof faces could stop street-driven PCG regeneration with a zero edge length.
notes: New builds target **UE 5.8 only**. The UE 5.5-5.7 downloads stay available as legacy versions and receive no further updates.
AI tools need Unreal's experimental Model Context Protocol plugin with Toolset Registry and Python support. Ordinary editing does not.
Bakes made before 6.1 have no preset tracking or surface tags. Rebake them once before sampling their floors and roofs in PCG.

summary: Undo fixes for spline command buttons.
highlights: Mirror, Flatten, Reverse, Gridify, and Apply Mirror To Spline buttons in the Details panel can now be undone with one Ctrl+Z. Before, undo skipped the button and reverted the edit made before it.
The Streets Network Details panel no longer shows the raw node and edge arrays.

summary: The v6 rewrite: Architect Mode, the Preset Library, baking, Streets, and the SA PCG node family.
highlights: Architect Mode for drawing and editing every Spline Architect actor in the viewport.
Preset Library for saving and reusing Wall, Building, and Curve setups.
Live preview while you edit, with explicit Bake and Rebake for persistent output.
Streets Network and Lot Zone actors with Streets Mode (UE 5.8).
The SA PCG node family for driving cities from Spline Architect data (UE 5.8).
See [Migrate from v5 to v6](/reference/migration-v6) when upgrading an existing project.
